Heatmap of genes across cells or groups

Source: R/heatmap.R
DoHeatmap_bioToolkit.Rd

Shows the expression of genes (e.g. top markers of each cell type) across cells, or across group means, z-scored per gene by default. Columns are arranged in blocks (`split.by`, e.g. cell type) and, within them, groups compared with each other (`group.by`, e.g. condition) marked by a coloured dot or strip. A drop-in alternative to Seurat::DoHeatmap() that reads any gene (not only those in "scale.data"), keeps small groups visible by downsampling, and has a fixed size. Save it with save_plot; the values behind it are returned by export_source_data.

Usage

DoHeatmap_bioToolkit(
  object,
  features,
  group.by = NULL,
  split.by = NULL,
  cells = NULL,
  assay = NULL,
  slot = "data",
  columns = c("cells", "groups"),
  average = c("linear", "log"),
  max.cells = 200,
  scale = TRUE,
  min.cutoff = NA,
  max.cutoff = NA,
  group.marker = c("dot", "strip", "none"),
  group.cols = NULL,
  annotations = NULL,
  annotation.cols = NULL,
  cols = NULL,
  label.features = NULL,
  label.side = c("right", "left"),
  feature.group.cols = NULL,
  split.by.cols = NULL,
  group.bar.width = 3.5,
  italic.genes = TRUE,
  panel.width = 6,
  cell.width = 0.18,
  cell.height = 0.13,
  panel.height = NULL,
  split.gap = 0.04,
  seed = 42,
  legend.position = c("right", "bottom", "top", "left", "none"),
  bg = "transparent"
)

Arguments

object

A Seurat object

features

Genes (or other numeric features, e.g. module scores) as rows: a character vector, or a named list of character vectors (e.g. from top_markers), drawn as blocks of rows named by the list. Genes not in the assay are left out with a warning

group.by

Metadata column of the groups compared (e.g. condition), marked by a coloured dot or strip above the columns. If NULL (default), the active identities

split.by

Metadata column of a higher-level grouping (e.g. cell type), drawn like facets: one named block of columns per level. If NULL (default), the groups are the blocks

cells

Cells to use, as names or indices. If NULL (default), all

assay

Assay to read genes from. If NULL (default), the default assay. The assay and layer used are reported in a message and written to the source data

slot

Layer to read, default is "data" (log-normalized values, all genes). "scale.data" is drawn as stored (`scale` is then not applied); it usually holds only the variable genes

columns

What a column is: "cells" (default; one column per cell, at most `max.cells` per group in each block) or "groups" (one column per group in each block: the group's mean)

average

How group means are computed from the log-normalized "data" layer (`columns = "groups"`): "linear" (default, log1p(mean(expm1(x))), as Seurat) or "log" (mean(x)), as in DotPlot_bioToolkit

max.cells

Largest number of cells drawn per group in each block, picked at random (`seed`), default is 200. NULL draws all cells. Only for `columns = "cells"`

scale

Whether to z-score each feature, default is TRUE: across all plotted cells (before downsampling) for `columns = "cells"`, across the columns for `columns = "groups"`

min.cutoff, max.cutoff

Ends of the colour scale: a number, a quantile of the plotted values such as "q5" / "q95", or NA (default). For z-scores, NA gives +-min(largest |z|, 2.5); for values that are all positive, 0 and the largest value; for other values, +-largest |value|. Values beyond the ends get the colour of the end

group.marker

How the groups are marked above the columns: "dot" (default), "strip" or "none"

group.cols

Colours of the groups: NULL (default) for the colours DimPlot_bioToolkit gives them, a qualitative palette name, or colours named by group

annotations

Further discrete metadata columns shown as colour strips above the columns (e.g. "sample"), each with its legend. With `columns = "groups"`, each must have one value per column. Cells in a group are ordered by the first one

annotation.cols

Colours of `annotations`: a list named by column, each a qualitative palette name or colours named by value. Columns not in the list get "tol-muted", "okabe-ito", "tol-light", ... in turn (or the default group colours when they have too many values)

cols

Colours of the heatmap. If NULL (default), for z-scores or signed values: "teal-yellow" (teal - black - yellow) with `columns = "cells"`, "blue-magenta" (light centre) with `columns = "groups"`; "magma" for unscaled non-negative values. Otherwise a palette name (see show_palettes) or colours from low to high, e.g. `c(low, mid, high)`

label.features

Which feature names are drawn: NULL (default) all of them if a row is tall enough for the text (at least 0.125 in), else none; TRUE or FALSE for all or none; or a few features, named with leader lines

label.side

Side of the feature names: "right" (default) or "left". Names of blocks of features are on the other side

feature.group.cols

Colours of the bars marking the blocks of features (a named list of `features`): NULL (default) for black bars, a qualitative palette name, or colours named by block

split.by.cols

Colours of the bars marking the blocks of columns (`split.by`, or the groups without it): NULL (default) for black bars, a qualitative palette name, or colours named by block

group.bar.width

Thickness of the block bars in points, default is 3.5

italic.genes

Whether gene names are set in italics, default is TRUE (genomic regions such as peaks never are)

panel.width

Width of the heatmap in inches for `columns = "cells"` (without the gaps between blocks), default is 6

cell.width

Width of one column in inches for `columns = "groups"`, default is 0.18

cell.height

Height of one row in inches, default is 0.13, which fits the names. Used while the heatmap is at most 6 in tall; beyond that, see `panel.height`

panel.height

Height of the heatmap in inches (without the gaps between blocks of features). If NULL (default), rows of `cell.height`, up to 6 in in all

split.gap

Gap between blocks of columns in inches, default is 0.04

seed

Random seed of the downsampling and cell order, default is 42

legend.position

Position of the legends: "right" (default), "bottom", "top", "left" or "none"

bg

Background colour, default is "transparent"

Value

A patchwork (body, header rows and labels)

Details

Cells without a value of `group.by` or `split.by` are left out, with a message. A feature with the same value in every cell has no z-score and is drawn at 0, with a message.

The source data (export_source_data) hold one row per column and feature: the `column` (cell, or group mean), `block`, `group`, `split`, the `annotations`, `feature_group`, `feature`, `value` (as read, or the group mean), `value_scaled` (when scaled), `n_cells` (group means) and the `assay`, `layer` and `average` used.

See also

top_markers, DotPlot_bioToolkit, save_plot, export_source_data

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
markers <- top_markers(Seurat::FindAllMarkers(obj, only.pos = TRUE), n = 5)

# Cells, z-scored per gene, at most 200 per cell type
DoHeatmap_bioToolkit(obj, markers, group.by = "cell_type", assay = "SCT")

# Group means: conditions (dots) compared within each cell type (blocks)
p <- DoHeatmap_bioToolkit(obj, markers, group.by = "condition",
                          split.by = "cell_type", columns = "groups")
save_plot(p, "heatmap.pdf")

# Many genes: names hidden, a few named with leader lines
DoHeatmap_bioToolkit(obj, top_markers(all_markers, n = 30), group.by = "cell_type",
                     label.features = c("Col1a1", "Cdh5", "Myh6"))
} # }
